disputed: There is no evidence the war was launched to benefit oil companies. The windfall is a market effect of a supply shock, and oil companies say high-price periods offset low-price ones. The point documented here is who profited and who paid, not motive.

items: Q2 2026: ExxonMobil profit doubled to $14.53 billion; Chevron's nearly quadrupled to $12.07 billion. Six European majors made a combined $22 billion in Q1, up 40%. Refiners gained the most. (PBS/AP (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/major-oil-companies-reap-massive-profits-as-u-s-and-iran-fighting-drives-energy-prices-higher))

Brent went from about $70 to above $100, peaking at $126 in March-May. US gasoline hit $4.11 a gallon in late July, about $1 higher than a year earlier. Shortages forced fuel rationing and closures abroad. (PBS/AP (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/major-oil-companies-reap-massive-profits-as-u-s-and-iran-fighting-drives-energy-prices-higher); Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/8/4/why-are-oil-companies-posting-record-profits-amid-iran-war-disruption))

Democrats proposed a windfall-profits tax. The Senate report notes fossil-fuel companies paid more to shareholders in 2025 than total direct US extreme-weather damages that year. (PBS/AP (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/major-oil-companies-reap-massive-profits-as-u-s-and-iran-fighting-drives-energy-prices-higher); Senate EPW Democrats (https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/press-releases-democratic?ID=D17E87C8-BA5B-4D3A-BA7A-CAD03C4B6F2D))

summary: The US–Iran war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed Brent crude above $100, peaking at $126. US oil majors posted their biggest profits in years while US gasoline rose about $1 a gallon.
title: Iran war oil shock: record oil profits, higher prices for everyone else
